title: bicountbrms: Custom brms Families for Paired Counts
description:
Custom brms families for Bayesian modelling of pairs of counts recorded on the same unit by two sources, such as two observers, two instruments, or two reporting channels. The pair is modelled by trivariate reduction: each count is the sum of a latent count recorded by both sources (the shared component) and a latent count recorded by that source alone (the source-exclusive component). The bipois family has Poisson components, and the binegbin family has negative-binomial components with a separate dispersion for each component.

Each family has two constructors. bipois() and binegbin() fit designs in which both sources record a count on every unit. bipois_partialobs() and binegbin_partialobs() also fit partially paired designs, in which source 1 has missing values. An unpaired row, on which only source 2 recorded a count, contributes the marginal probability of that count to the likelihood, so the unpaired row informs the shared component and the exclusive component of source 2. posterior_predict_y1_given_y2() imputes the missing counts of source 1 conditional on the counts recorded by source 2, and posterior_predict_y1_and_y2() draws both counts together. The standard brms post-processing functions, including posterior_predict(), pp_check(), and loo(), apply without modification.

The model can be fitted in its native parameters, the rates and dispersions of the three latent components, or in the congruence–bias coordinates: the midpoint of the two expected counts, the congruence between the two sources, the source bias, and, for binegbin, the overdispersion of each component. bf_mfd() writes the brms formula in the congruence–bias coordinates, so that priors and predictors act directly on the midpoint, the congruence, and the source bias. mfd_to_dpars() and dpars_to_mfd() convert between the native parameters and the congruence–bias coordinates, and rbicount() simulates pairs of counts from the model.

Documentation: https://anhsmith.github.io/bicountbrms/
